notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2022, as the city reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
Public schools are run by separate school districts, so they are not included. Residents also pay Perry County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Arkansas city candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
Cameras: no license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Perryville's borders in OpenStreetMap as of 2026-10-20.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Arkansas yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.
